cards.en: How do you do? (very formal, first meeting)
Please take care of me. / I look forward to working with you.
Welcome. (said to someone who comes in)

quiz.q: You meet your new boss for the first time. What is the best thing to say?
quiz.why: 처음 뵙겠습니다 is the formal way to greet someone you meet for the first time.

quiz.q: A customer walks into your shop. What do you say?
quiz.why: 어서 오세요 means welcome. The shop says it to the person who comes in.

quiz.q: 저는 일본에서 왔어요 means:
quiz.why: -에서 왔어요 means came from. 일본에서 = from Japan.

quiz.q: Which question asks about someone's nationality?
quiz.why: 어느 나라 사람이에요? literally asks which country person you are.

quiz.q: Before bed, you say good night to your grandmother.
quiz.why: 안녕히 주무세요 is the respectful form of good night for an older person.

fill.en: Nice to meet you.
I came from the USA.
What is your name?
Please take care of me.
Welcome.

quiz.q: Which letter makes the 'm' sound in Korean?
quiz.why: ㅁ (미음) represents the m sound, as in 모자 (hat).

quiz.q: Which of the following is a horizontal vowel written below the consonant?
quiz.why: ㅗ is a horizontal vowel and is positioned directly underneath the initial consonant, like in 고.

quiz.q: When ㅇ is used at the beginning of a syllable block (like in 오), what sound does it make?
opts: It is silent and serves as a placeholder.
quiz.why: At the beginning of a syllable, ㅇ has no sound and simply holds the space for the vowel.

quiz.q: What syllable is formed by combining the consonant ㄱ and the vowel ㅏ?
quiz.why: ㄱ (g/k) plus vertical vowel ㅏ (a) forms the syllable block 가 (ga).

quiz.q: What is the official Korean name for the consonant letter ㄴ?
quiz.why: The consonant ㄴ is officially called 니은 (nieun).

fill.en: The name of consonant ㄱ is giyeok.

fill.q: 자음 ㅂ과 모음 ㅏ가 만나면 ___가 됩니다.
fill.en: When consonant ㅂ and vowel ㅏ meet, it becomes ba.
The first syllable of the word haneul (sky) is ha.
The official name of the Hangul consonant ㄴ is nieun.

fill.q: 자음 ㅅ과 모음 ㅗ를 결합하면 ___가 됩니다.
fill.en: Combining consonant ㅅ and vowel ㅗ creates so.

cards.en: final consonant (batchim at the bottom of a block)
liaison (carrying a batchim over to a following vowel)

quiz.q: How many representative batchim sounds exist when final consonants are pronounced in isolation?
quiz.why: All Korean final consonants collapse into one of 7 representative sounds: [ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ].

quiz.q: What representative sound does the final consonant in 옷 (clothes) make when spoken alone?
quiz.why: The letter ㅅ simplifies to the representative stop sound [ㄷ] at the end of a syllable.

quiz.q: According to the liaison rule (연음), how is the phrase 부엌에 pronounced?
quiz.why: The final consonant ㅋ moves into the silent ㅇ of 에, so 부엌에 is read [부어케].

quiz.q: Which of the following words ends with the [ㅂ] representative sound when spoken alone?
quiz.why: 밥 ends with ㅂ, which is pronounced as the representative bilabial stop [ㅂ].

quiz.q: How is the phrase 집에 (to home) pronounced in natural spoken Korean?
quiz.why: Due to liaison, the final ㅂ carries over into the following vowel 에, producing [지베].

fill.en: Reading practice: the sound of 꽃이 is [kkochi].
The sound of 밖에 is [bakke].
The representative batchim sound of the word ip (leaf) is [ㅂ].

fill.q: 꽃 한 송이를 발음할 때 받침 소리는 [___]으로 바뀝니다.
fill.en: When pronouncing a flower (꽃), the final consonant changes to [ㄷ].
The sound of 닫는 is [danneun].

cards.en: do not have / there is no

quiz.q: Which ending should you attach to a noun ending in a vowel to say 'is' (e.g., 의사)?
quiz.why: Nouns ending in a vowel attach -예요 without a particle (의사예요).

quiz.q: How do you say 'I am not a student' in polite Korean?
quiz.why: To negate identity, attach 이/가 아니에요 to the noun: 학생이 아니에요.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly expresses 'I have an umbrella'?
quiz.why: Possession of an object uses Noun + 이/가 있어요: 우산이 있어요.

quiz.q: What particle is used before 아니에요, 있어요, and 없어요?
quiz.why: 아니에요, 있어요, and 없어요 all require the subject particle 이/가 on the preceding noun.

quiz.q: What does 지갑에 돈이 없어요 mean?
opts: I have no money in my wallet.
There is money in the wallet.
quiz.why: 돈이 없어요 means there is no money / I do not have money.

fill.en: My job is an office worker.
I am not a singer.
There is a key in my pocket right now.
I am thirsty, but there is no water to drink.
The person over there is a kind nurse.

cards.en: that over there (modifier far from both)

quiz.q: Which word would you use to refer to a pen sitting right beside the listener?
quiz.why: 그 refers to items close to the listener or already mentioned in conversation.

quiz.q: What is the common spoken contraction of 이것이 (this thing as subject)?
quiz.why: 이것이 contracts to 이게 in natural everyday speech.

quiz.q: You want to say 'Please sit here' pointing to a chair next to you. Which word means 'here'?
quiz.why: 여기 means 'here' (the place near the speaker).

quiz.q: When both you and your friend are looking at a distant building across the river, which word should you use?
quiz.why: 저 is used for people or objects visible but distant from both speaker and listener.

quiz.q: How do native speakers naturally say 'What is that (near you)?' in spoken Korean?
quiz.why: 그게 (short for 그것이) refers to an item near the listener.

fill.q: 제 손에 들고 있는 ___ 사과는 정말 달아요.
fill.en: This apple that I am holding in my hand is really sweet.

fill.q: 책상 위에 놓인 ___ 모자는 누구 거예요?
fill.en: Whose is that hat on the desk?

fill.q: 멀리 보이는 ___ 비행기가 참 높이 날고 있어요.
fill.en: That airplane visible far away is flying very high.

fill.q: 처음 오셨으면 편한 자리에 앉아 ___서 기다려 주세요.
fill.en: If it is your first time here, please sit in a comfortable seat and wait here.

fill.q: 식당 종업원을 부를 때 공손하게 '___요!'라고 말해요.
fill.en: When calling a restaurant server, we politely say 'Excuse me (over there)!'

cards.en: location particle where action happens (at / in)

quiz.q: Which object particle attaches to a noun ending in a consonant, such as 책 (book)?
quiz.why: Nouns ending in a batchim take 을 as the direct object particle (책을).

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly describes studying inside the library?
quiz.why: Use 에서 for the location where an active event (like studying) takes place.

quiz.q: You are traveling to school by subway. Which particle means 'by' (transportation)?
quiz.why: Nouns ending in ㄹ take 로 directly without inserting 으: 지하철 + 로 = 지하철로.

quiz.q: How do you say 'I eat bread and milk' using the formal connecting particle 과/와?
quiz.why: 빵 ends in batchim ㅇ, so it takes 과: 빵과 우유.

quiz.q: Which particle specifies an exact meeting time, such as 'at 3 o'clock'?
quiz.why: Specific time points take the static particle 에 (3시에 만나요).

fill.en: My younger sibling washes fresh apples every morning.
I drank warm green tea for breakfast.

fill.q: 내일 오후 두 시___ 교실에서 회의가 시작돼요.
fill.en: The meeting starts at 2 PM tomorrow in the classroom.
Our family eats dinner in the living room.

fill.q: 부산까지 빠른 기차___ 이동하면 두 시간 걸려요.
fill.en: If you travel by fast train to Busan, it takes two hours.

quiz.q: When 누구 (who) is combined with the subject particle 가, how is it correctly written?
quiz.why: When 누구 acts as the subject with particle 가, it must always contract to 누가.

quiz.q: Which question word asks about location ('where')?
quiz.why: 어디 specifically asks about places or locations.

quiz.q: Which word is used to ask for the price of an item in Korean (e.g., 'How much is this?')?
quiz.why: 얼마 is used to ask about monetary prices: 이거 얼마예요? (How much is this?).

quiz.q: Which question asks 'What time is it right now?' using counter word 시 (o'clock)?
quiz.why: 몇 is used directly before counter nouns: 지금 몇 시예요? (What time is it now?).

quiz.q: How do you ask someone 'Why are you learning Korean?'
quiz.why: 왜 asks for the reason or purpose behind an action ('Why').

fill.en: Where is the hometown of the newly transferred student?
When is the starting time for tomorrow's birthday party?
What do you want to eat for lunch today?

fill.q: 방과 후에 운동장에서 축구를 한 사람은 ___예요?
fill.en: Who is the person who played soccer on the field after school?
How long does it take walking from the subway station to the office?

quiz.q: Which ending attaches to the stem of 좋다 (좋-)?
quiz.why: The stem vowel of 좋다 is ㅗ, so it takes -아요 to become 좋아요.

quiz.q: What is the correct polite present form of 배우다 (to learn)?
quiz.why: The stem vowel is ㅜ, which combines with -어요 into -워요 (배워요).

quiz.q: What is the polite present form of 노래하다 (to sing)?
quiz.why: Verbs ending in 하다 always change to 해요 in the polite present tense.

quiz.q: Which verb conjugates with -어요?
quiz.why: 열다 has the stem vowel ㅕ, so it takes -어요 (열어요). The others have ㅏ and take -아요.

quiz.q: What is the polite present form of 보다 (to see / watch)?
quiz.why: 보- combines with -아요 to contract into 봐요.

fill.en: I drink juice in the morning.
I see a puppy in the park.
I meet the teacher in the classroom.
I exercise diligently every morning.
I buy delicious apples at the market.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 크다 (big)?
quiz.why: 작다 means small, which is the opposite of 크다 (big).

quiz.q: What is the polite present form of 크다 (to be big)?
quiz.why: When the stem vowel ㅡ is dropped without another vowel, it conjugates as 커요.

quiz.q: Which word means to be busy?
quiz.why: 바쁘다 means to be busy. Its polite form is 바빠요.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 맛있다 (delicious)?
quiz.why: 맛없다 means not delicious, the direct opposite of 맛있다.

quiz.q: What is the polite present form of 만나다 (to meet)?
quiz.why: 만나- ends in vowel ㅏ, so adding -아요 contracts naturally to 만나요.

fill.en: This bag is really big. (크다)
Because there is a lot of work at the office, I am very busy. (바쁘다)
There are very many people in the library. (많다)
The subway station is very close to home. (가깝다)
The Korean exam is easier than expected. (쉽다)

cards.en: o clock (used with Native Korean numbers)

quiz.q: Which counter is used for cats and dogs?
quiz.why: 마리 is the counter for animals like cats, dogs, and birds.

quiz.q: How do you say one cup of green tea in Korean?
quiz.why: Before a counter, 하나 changes to 한, so one cup is 한 잔.

quiz.q: Which number system is used for minutes (분)?
quiz.why: Hours (시) use Native Korean numbers, but minutes (분) use Sino-Korean numbers.

quiz.q: How do you read 10,000 won in Korean?
quiz.why: 10,000 in Sino-Korean is 만, so 10,000 won is 만 원.

quiz.q: What happens to 둘 when placed right before a counter?
quiz.why: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷 shorten to 한, 두, 세, 네 when placed directly before a counter.

fill.en: There are three guests in the restaurant.
Please give me two glasses of cold juice at the cafe.
There is one cute puppy in the park.
Right now it is 5:30 in the afternoon.
This T-shirt is 20,000 won.

quiz.q: How do you pronounce June (6월) in Korean?
quiz.why: The final consonant drops before 월, so June is pronounced and written as 유월.

quiz.q: How do you pronounce October (10월) in Korean?
quiz.why: The final consonant drops before 월, so October is written and spoken as 시월.

quiz.q: Which day of the week is Wednesday?
quiz.why: 수요일 is Wednesday (수 represents water).

quiz.q: If today is Friday (금요일), what day is tomorrow (내일)?
quiz.why: The day after Friday (금요일) is Saturday (토요일).

quiz.q: What does 모레 mean in English?
quiz.why: 모레 means the day after tomorrow. Tomorrow is 내일.

fill.en: I rest on the weekend, Saturday and Sunday.
Children s Day is May 5th.
Hangul Day is October 9th.
Since today is Wednesday, yesterday was Tuesday.
Since this week is busy, let s meet next weekend.

quiz.q: A female speaker calls her older brother:
quiz.why: A female speaker calls her older brother 오빠. A male speaker calls his older brother 형.

quiz.q: A male speaker calls his older sister:
quiz.why: A male speaker calls his older sister 누나. A female speaker calls her older sister 언니.

quiz.q: What is the polite honorific word for 이름 (name)?
quiz.why: 성함 is the respectful honorific term for an elder person s name.

quiz.q: What is the honorific partner of the verb 자다 (to sleep)?
quiz.why: 주무시다 is the honorific verb for to sleep (자다).

quiz.q: What is the respectful subject particle replacing 이/가 for elders?
quiz.why: 께서 is the honorific subject particle (replacing 이/가), while 께 is the dative particle (to someone).

fill.en: What is your grandfather s name? (respectful form of 이름)
How old is the elderly person? (respectful form of 나이)
I have one younger brother and one younger sister.
I gave a thank-you card to my teacher. (honorific to)
Mother is reading a book in the living room. (honorific subject particle)

quiz.q: Which position word means behind or in the back?
quiz.why: 뒤 means behind or back. 앞 means in front.

quiz.q: Where do you go to buy medicine in Korea?
quiz.why: 약국 is pharmacy, where you purchase medicine.

quiz.q: Where do you deposit or withdraw money?
quiz.why: 은행 means bank.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 있어요 (there is / to have)?
quiz.why: 없어요 means there is not or to not have, the direct opposite of 있어요.

quiz.q: Which word means inside?
quiz.why: 안 means inside. 밖 means outside.

fill.en: The teacher is standing in front of the board.
There is a large bookstore next to the subway station.
Small slippers are placed under the bed.
Because I caught a cold, I go to the pharmacy to buy medicine.
Right now there is no cash at all in my wallet.

quiz.q: What color is a ripe banana (바나나)?
quiz.why: A banana is yellow, which is 노란색 in Korean.

quiz.q: What is the three-sided triangle shape called in everyday Korean?
quiz.why: 세모 is the everyday word for triangle (세 means three).

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 무겁다 (heavy)?
quiz.why: 가볍다 means light in weight, which is the opposite of 무겁다.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 빠르다 (fast) in the polite present tense?
quiz.why: The opposite of 빠르다 (fast) is 느리다 (slow), which conjugates to 느려요.

quiz.q: What color is clean snow (눈)?
quiz.why: Snow is white, which is 흰색 or 하얀색.

fill.en: The stop light on the traffic signal is red.
The sea and the sky are a refreshing blue.
Because this box is made of paper, it is very light. (가볍다)
The shape of the window is a neat square / rectangle.
In a running race, the cheetah is really fast. (빠르다)

quiz.q: Where do you cook food in a home?
quiz.why: 부엌 is the kitchen, where meals are prepared and cooked.

quiz.q: Which appliance is used to wash dirty clothes?
quiz.why: 세탁기 is the washing machine.

quiz.q: Where do Koreans typically take off their shoes when entering a house?
quiz.why: 현관 is the front entrance where shoes are removed.

quiz.q: Which piece of furniture do you sleep on?
quiz.why: 침대 means bed.

quiz.q: Where do family members usually gather to watch TV?
quiz.why: 거실 is the living room, typically where the TV and sofa are placed.

fill.en: Family members sit around the dining table when having a meal.
I gather dirty socks and clothes and put them in the washing machine.
Getting up in the morning, I open the bedroom window wide. (열다)

fill.q: 새로 산 외투를 옷걸이에 걸어서 ___에 넣었어요.
fill.en: I hung the newly bought coat on a hanger and put it in the wardrobe.

fill.q: 퇴근하고 집에 오면 편안한 ___에 앉아서 쉬어요.
fill.en: Coming home after work, I sit on the comfortable sofa and rest.

quiz.q: What does the teacher mean by 책을 펴세요?
quiz.why: 책을 펴세요 means Please open your book (펴다 means to open or unfold).

quiz.q: When the teacher speaks too fast, what is the best polite request?
quiz.why: 천천히 말씀해 주세요 politely asks Please speak slowly.

quiz.q: What tool do you use to erase pencil writing?
quiz.why: 지우개 means eraser (from 지우다 to erase).

quiz.q: What does 따라 읽으세요 mean?
quiz.why: 따라 읽으세요 means Please read after me / repeat after me.

quiz.q: How do you politely say I understand to your teacher?
quiz.why: 알겠습니다 is the formal polite acknowledgment meaning Understood / I understand.

fill.en: Since class is starting, everyone please open your books.

fill.q: 필통 안에 연필과 볼펜이 세 자루 ___.
fill.en: There are three pencils and ballpoint pens inside the pencil case.
The teacher writes an important word on the board. (쓰다)
Because pronunciation is difficult, I listen carefully to the teacher s voice. (듣다)
Because class ended, I put the textbook in my bag. (넣다)

quiz.q: How do you call a server over at a Korean restaurant?
quiz.why: 저기요 or 여기요 is used to politely get the server s attention.

quiz.q: What does 계산해 주세요 mean when finishing a meal?
opts: Check, please. / Please give me the bill.
quiz.why: 계산해 주세요 asks the cashier or server for the bill/check.

quiz.q: Which word describes the taste of hot spicy kimchi stew (김치찌개)?
quiz.why: Kimchi stew is typically spicy, which is 맵다 (매워요 in polite present).

quiz.q: Which counter is used to order servings of barbecue meat (고기)?
quiz.why: 인분 is the counter for food portions or servings per person.

quiz.q: What is the polite present form of 달다 (to be sweet)?
quiz.why: 달다 conjugates with -아요 into 달아요.

fill.en: Before ordering, please show me the menu first.
Please give me two servings of galbi and two bowls of rice.

fill.q: 이 국은 간이 맞지 않아서 조금 ___.
fill.en: This soup lacks seasoning so it is a bit bland. (싱겁다)

fill.q: 소금을 너무 많이 넣어서 국물이 너무 ___.
fill.en: Because too much salt was added, the broth is too salty. (짜다)
Chocolate and ice cream are very sweet. (달다)
